comparison.question: on the only corpus a held-out evaluation permits -- the 3 phase-1 solutions -- does stitch find anything Archaeon's repeated-subtree extractor does not?
comparison.answer: NO, AND NEITHER DOES THEIRS. Both return an EMPTY library on the legitimate corpus, and they agree for the same reason: three solutions of 2-4 grammar nodes contain no subexpression repeated across two of them. That is a fact about the corpus, not about either extractor, and no amount of tool quality changes it.

resource_receipt.rss_enforcement: NOT ENFORCED -- no job object / cgroup cap. peak_rss_bytes_os_counter is the OS peak-working-set counter for this process and IS reliable; rss_ceiling_exceeded_during_sampling is sampled and can miss a spike. Neither stops a step.
resource_receipt.rss_excludes_children: This is THIS process only. pip, git and venv run as children and their RSS is NOT included.

cancellation.measured_on_this_host: vivarium/tools/probe_process_tree_kill.py -> TREE REAPED (2026-09-11); re-run before admitting a backend on another host
cancellation.scope: This wrapper meters PREPARATION-time work (pip, git, cargo, the stitch binary). It is not an admitted in-run backend, and arming a job object does not make it one -- Vivarium's contract admits a backend, not a kill mechanism.

MEASURED, not assumed: whether stitch beats the extractor Archaeon already has, on the corpus a held-out evaluation permits
LEAKAGE IS REPORTED RATHER THAN EXPORTED: any component that is itself a held-out phase-2 solution is counted and its corpus marked not exportable
the verdict comes from VIVARIUM'S SEMANTIC checker over the full held-out task set, not from my string equality on s-expressions

verdict: stitch's library is EMPTY on the only corpus a held-out evaluation permits (3 phase-1 solutions), and Archaeon's existing extractor is empty on it too. On ALL_17 stitch returns 3 abstractions, of which 3 ARE held-out phase-2 solutions -- so that library is not exportable for phase-2 use. The export path itself works and the loader accepts it; there is nothing on this corpus worth putting through it.
